verdict.rationale: Teams documents first-party automation surfaces that can run outside the client UI. The Graph Teams API is meant for services that run outside the Teams user experience to automate Teams scenarios, such as creating teams and channels and posting messages. The Agents Toolkit CLI scripts provisioning, deployment, validation, packaging and publishing without the IDE. However, nothing in the evidence explicitly documents CI/CD pipeline usage or non-interactive authentication. Missing for 10: explicit CI/pipeline integration docs (e.g. non-interactive/service-principal auth for the CLI), a documented headless run mode, and independent hands-on corroboration of CI usage.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: You can create websites, services, and native platform applications that run outside the Microsoft Teams user experience, and call the Teams API to automate Teams scenarios.
These apps can also automate creating teams, channels, and conversations, enhancing the value of Microsoft Teams.
Agents Toolkit CLI offers the same features as the IDE extensions.
Resource Provisioning and Deployment: Provision necessary cloud resources and deploy your application to Azure.
Validation, Packaging, and Publishing: Validate, package, and publish your agent or application using CLI commands.
